Quick sync on onboarding progress, access provisioning, and environment readiness. Discussed initial latency/cost numbers from the pilot, a few tuning items (batching + kv cache), and next steps for security docs and on-prem readiness. Action items assigned.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call. I see Priya, Liam, Sana, Marco 
d
shanks. We'll keep to 30 mins but we have 40 set so room for Qs.
[01:12] Priya (NexaHead): Yeah hi, Priya here. We pulled last week's test results, wanted to go over a couple of anomalies 
d

d some tail latency spikes around long contexts.
[02:05] Marco (Redwood SE): cool, thanks. I pulled the same results; looks like the spikes correlate to sequence length > 1024 and fallback to single-token mode, might be a batching/kvcache thing, also our quantized variant shows better median but different tails.
[03:30] Liam (CTO): sorry to jump in, just to confirm are these tests on dedicated nodes or hosted? we wanted to measure both.
[03:45] Ava: current pilot run is on Redwood Dedicated reserved pool in us-west with 4 GPUs, plus a small hosted fallback for overflow. Marco, correct me if i butcher that.
[04:10] Marco: yep that's right. Dedicated for steady throughput, and a hosted path we've configured as a lower-cost fallback. We saw about 65-75ms median token latency on short prompts, long prompts hit 700-1,200ms on tails.
[04:45] Sana (Platform): those 700ms are a bit high for our interactive flows. Is there room to tune batching or kv cache to reduce that?
[05:02] Marco: definitely 
d

 two knobs: decrease max-batch delay and enable prefix KV caching aggressively for repeating contexts. Also switching to the 8-bit quantized runtime reduces memory pressure and can lower some tails but can slightly change output distribution.
[06:15] Priya: we saw differences in generation quality after quantizing, some hallucination rate changed. How do we evaluate quality regressions?
[06:40] Ava: we recommend running our eval harness on a fixed prompt set 
d
we have a baseline we can share, and Redwood Optimize will flag regressions. For the pilot, we can run a quality/latency sweep.
[07:20] Liam: also, security question 
d
we need to confirm KMS integration and audit logs retention. SOC2? SSO?
[07:35] Marco: Redwood Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations, and audit logs are available; we'll share the SOC 2 pack. For this pilot, you can provision a staging VPC and give us a service account, then we can deploy a Private control plane or dedicated nodes behind your VPC.
[08:05] Sana: ok good. On our side, infra will only accept traffic from specific IP ranges and via mTLS; can Redwood support that?
[08:20] Ava: yes, we can do mTLS and IP allow lists for Dedicated; for Private we can fit into your network. We'll send a checklist.
[09:02] Priya: back to performance 
d
c an we get end-to-end p90/p99 numbers for the full pipeline (app -> redwood -> response)?
[09:25] Marco: we'll run an end-to-end benchmark using your sample logs; need staging kube context and service account. With current numbers, p90 is ~850ms on long sequences, p99 closer to 1.2s. After KV caching and smaller batch delay we expect p90 to drop toward ~500-600ms.
[10:40] Liam: any tradeoffs on cost when enabling aggressive kv cache?
[10:55] Marco: KV cache increases memory usage per replica; that pushes up the instance footprint and cost, but reduces per-token compute since repeated context doesn't recompute. So it's latency vs infra cost tradeoff. Redwood Optimize can give recommendations by workload.
[12:00] Priya: curious about routing 
d
c an we route sensitive traffic to Private and non-sensitive to Hosted to balance cost?
[12:20] Ava: absolutely. Smart routing policy supports routing by tag/route/region 
d
you can pin sensitive routes to Private or Dedicated and overflow to Hosted for lower-sensitivity requests.
[13:05] Sana: on credentials, what's the minimum we need to give you to run a benchmark?
[13:20] Marco: staging service account with read/write to a test namespace, kubeconfig or context, and a sample dataset (anonymized). We'll only run load generators from our side into the cluster.
[14:00] Priya: i'll follow up with logs, but one more question 
d
competitor comparison, we tested Anthropic earlier; their p99 was lower but cost higher, and vendor lock-in was a concern.
[14:20] Ava: makes sense, we often see that tradeoff. Redwood aims to keep you flexible (same API across environments) and reduce per-token cost via batching and caching.
[15:10] Liam: procurement note 
d
we may need a pilot addendum to the MSA for data residency and limited exposure. Ava can you send that?
[15:25] Ava: yes i'll send a pilot addendum and pricing sheet.
[16:00] Marco: quick note on the anomaly Priya saw 
d
i think it's a case where the batcher flush policy sent a partially filled batch leading to a high tail. We'll tweak max latency and add warm-up runs, then re-run the test.
[17:10] Priya: ok good. Can you also share the exact model variant used in the run? one of our data scientists wants to see hyperparams.
[17:25] Marco: that run used rwinx-2b-quant-v2 (note, transcript may misname), sequence cap 2048, beam=1, temp 0.2. i'll share the exact config.
[18:40] Sana: about on-prem 
d
our security team is strict but interested. what is the typical timeline to get Private control-plane deployed in our VPC?
[19:02] Marco: from signed order + infra creds it's typically 2-4 weeks for standard cases; if air-gapped there is additional time for on-prem packaging. We can start with Dedicated while we work on Private readiness.
[20:10] Liam: do you support SAML SSO and RBAC mapping to our IdP?
[20:25] Ava: yes SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning supported; we'll send the SSO checklist.
[21:00] Priya: one more performance ask 
d
can you run a focused test with a higher concurrency pattern to simulate peak traffic (200 rps) and show token cost numbers?
[21:20] Marco: yes, we can run 200 rps synthetic and show cost per 1k tokens 
d
but need your sample workload to be realistic.
[22:35] Sana: note from our infra lead: we need to whitelist Redwood egress IPs for monitoring hooks.
[22:48] Ava: we'll include the IP list in the checklist.
[24:00] Marco: i'll also include recommended batch and cache settings we plan to apply and expected impact numbers.
[25:15] Priya: what's the best way to share results back to our team? a short summary + spreadsheet?
[25:30] Ava: yes spreadsheet with p50/p90/p99, token cost estimates, and config diffs. we'll upload to the shared drive and post a link in the pilot slack channel.
[26:50] Liam: any blockers from Redwood side to run the next benchmark?
[27:05] Marco: need the kubecontext + staging service account and anonymized logs. after that we can run a benchmark within 48 hours.
[28:30] Priya: we'll aim to have the artifacts by Friday (2027-10-01).
[29:10] Ava: great. quick recap 
d
Ava to send pricing/addendum, Marco to provision staging creds and run a tuning pass, Nexa to share logs and whitelist IPs. Next call: tentatively 2027-10-06 to review tuned results.
[30:00] Sana: sounds good. small nit, can you add the security contact for Redwood to the calendar invite?
[30:10] Ava: yes, adding security + solutions engineering.
[31:00] Priya: one question on billing 
d
if we overflow to hosted, how is cost attributed? per-token and billed to the pilot account, right?
[31:18] Ava: correct, overflow tokens billed to the pilot project; we can show per-route breakdowns in the console.
[32:30] Marco: last technical note 
d
we'll enable prefix caching and reduce max-batch-ms from 40 to 20 for the next run; that should reduce tail latency but may increase per-token CPU usage slightly.
[33:40] Liam: ok let's try it. any other items?
[33:55] Priya: none. thanks everyone.
[34:20] Ava: thanks all, we'll send notes.
[34:40] Meeting end (call dropped into wrap).
